the pharmacokinetic data available to date do not justify the use of etravirine or maraviroc in pregnancy, but raltegravir and neviraprine should be considered safe and effective options.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleoside reverse transcriptases inhibitors, non-nucleosidic reverse transcriptase inhibitors and the integrase inhibitor, raltegravir have a high accumulation ratio in the placenta.

the placenta and amniotic fluid may serve as anatomical sanctuary sites for the fetus, and that the pharmacological characteristics of antiretroval drugs may influence their ability to penetrate the fetal compartment.
the nucleoside analogs and nevirapines accumulate in the fetal compartment, while protease inhibitors and the newer antiretroviruses have low to moderate accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the placenta is a barrier to antiretrovials and that the accumulation ratio is not always a good surrogate of placental transfer.

the placental transfer of antiretrovilals is a complex phenomenon, influenced by maternal and fetal factors, and that the placenta is not just a passive barrier to drug transfer, but an active organ of drug metabolism.
antiretrovials are generally well absorbed by the fetus and placenta, but the degree of placental accumulation differs significantly among the various drug classes.
